newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher in token volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher in token volume.

text.p: Argentine stocks staged a mild-mannered reversal Friday and closed higher in token turnover, cheered by hopes the government may seek to ease labor laws, dealers said.

"Today there was talk of measures to rekindle the economy -- it seems the government will try to compensate for new proposed tax hikes with lower labor costs, and this hope may spur fresh gains on the bolsa Monday when Wall Street is closed", said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV jumped 1.0 percent to 509.43, boosting the weekly tally of gains to 1.8 percent.
The rise trimmed losses in August to 3.7 percent.
The market managed to buck another slump on Wall Street, rattled since Thursday by a raft of surprisingly strong economic data.
However if U.S. long bond yields resumed their upward march Tuesday then the bolsa might see a backlash, dealers said.
Floor volume slowed to an extremely weak 11 million pesos in the session from 11.8 million Thursday, while over the counter deals grew to 75.7 million pesos against 52.5 million Thursday.
"The scant bidding is keeping prices stuck in fairly narrow ranges, but the good thing about the lack of volume is that it halted the recent fall," said Bonanno.
Analysts did not expect activity to pick up until Congress passes a controversial package of tax reforms announced nearly three weeks ago by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, who took office July 29.
"Nobody knows exactly what's happening with the measures and this uncertainty is hurting the markets," said Luis Enrique Alvarez of brokers Alvarez.

"Even in the best case scenario, if Congress had passed the package immediately, the tax hikes themselves wouldn't have cheered up investors," said Alvarez. "Measures like raising wealth tax and cutting export reimbursements obviously don't help risk investment. But in the beginning the markets would have been willing to shrug them off."
He noted the delay only compounded fears the tax hikes would hurt economic recovery without generating a much-needed rise in revenue.
The broad market index gained 0.9 percent Friday with winners thrasing losers 30 to 10 and 22 stocks closing flat.
Top main-tier gainers were construction stock Polledo, up 3.4 percent, and petrochemical concern Indupa and textile firm Alpargatas, both up 2.9 percent.
The only MerVal losers were carmaker Ciadea, real estate developer Irsa and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which fell 3.9 percent, 1.4 percent and 0.2 percent, respectively.
